purpose: Finerenone is used to protect the kidneys and heart in adults who have chronic kidney disease caused by type 2 diabetes. It helps slow down the worsening of kidney disease and lowers the risk of serious problems like kidney failure and heart-related events. Your doctor may prescribe it alongside other diabetes and kidney medications.
how_it_works: Your body has a hormone called aldosterone that, when overactive, can cause inflammation and scarring in your kidneys and heart. Finerenone blocks the receptors that aldosterone attaches to, which helps reduce that harmful inflammation and damage. Think of it like putting a shield over those receptors so the hormone cannot cause as much harm.
common_side_effects: The most common side effect is higher potassium levels in your blood (called hyperkalemia), which can sometimes cause muscle weakness or an irregular heartbeat. You may also notice a slight decrease in kidney function at first, lower blood pressure, or low sodium levels. Your doctor will do regular blood tests to keep an eye on your potassium and kidney function.
warnings: This medication can raise your potassium to dangerous levels, so do not use potassium supplements or salt substitutes containing potassium without asking your doctor first. It should NOT be taken during pregnancy as it can seriously harm an unborn baby — use reliable birth control if you could become pregnant. Tell your doctor about all other medications you take, especially certain antifungals or antibiotics, because some drugs can interact with finerenone and raise its levels in your blood to unsafe amounts.
typical_dosing: The usual starting dose is 10 mg taken by mouth once a day with or without food. After about 4 weeks, your doctor will check your potassium level and may increase your dose to 20 mg once daily if your potassium is in a safe range. Always take it at the same time each day and do not stop without talking to your doctor first.
